subject: SkyShop: API handshake latency & 5xx surge — escalation
messages:
From: Anna Li <anna@skyshop.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Nov 2028 09:12:03 -0800
Subject: Sharp latency + 5xx on /checkout — urgent

Rishi,

We just started seeing a big spike in latency and 5xx errors hitting /checkout at ~09:00 PST. Latency has tripled on average and 5xxs are ~10% of requests. This is directly impacting payment throughput (we're down ~40% for the last 30m).

What we've observed: 
- Errors: consistent 502/504s coming from your inference gateway (see attached sample logs)
- Timing: spike began ~09:00 and has persisted for >30m
- Workarounds attempted: failed over a subset of traffic to eu region (temporary improvement)

We need immediate help — our checkout traffic is revenue-critical. Attaching a short sample of server logs and a recorded request id.

Attachment: skyshop-checkout-5xx-sample.log (text/plain, 42KB)

---
Anna Li
Head of Payments // SkyShop
anna@skyshop.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Li <anna@skyshop.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Nov 2028 09:20:11 -0800
Subject: Re: Sharp latency + 5xx on /checkout — urgent

Anna — thanks for the alert and the log sample. We're treating this as a Sev1. I am looping in Monica (CS lead for high-impact infra incidents) and Vivek (ops exec) so we can move quickly.

Immediate plan (first 15m):
1) Monica: can you collect a traceroute and DNS query sample from your side?
2) We'll pull gateway metrics, recent deployment diffs, and edge proxy logs.
3) If it's path/DNS related we'll prepare an emergency peering/reroute plan and request permission to engage the cloud provider.

Please confirm: do you want us to go directly to the cloud provider and share the trace/pcap? That will make the provider triage faster.

Attaching: request id and I've created a HubSpot incident record.

Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HSK-3421

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Lead // Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Nov 2028 09:34:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Sharp latency + 5xx on /checkout — urgent

Quick triage notes (collected 09:25–09:33 PST):
- Traceroute (attached) from SkyShop front-end -> our edge shows an asymmetric path: two hops go via a third-party transit that is returning ICMP TTL-expired intermittently. Packet timeouts coincide with the 5xx windows.
- DNS: observed intermittent NXDOMAIN/timeout for the regional resolver; queries that succeed route via a different recursive group and latency improves. See attached dns-query-samples-1115.txt.
- Edge proxy: our edge logs show a surge of backend 502s and a spike in connection resets to an internal proxy (likely the NAT/proxy cluster at our peering edge).

Attachments: traceroute-skyshop-1115.txt (text/plain), dns-query-samples-1115.txt (text/plain)

Proposed immediate actions:
A) Ask SkyShop for permission to share pcap/traces with cloud provider and open a peering reroute ticket (preferred)
B) Short-term: shift SkyShop traffic to alternate edge POP (they reported eu region improved) — needs BGP community change or manual routing change on our side
C) If provider refuses, escalate to on-call network eng to apply proxy-level fallback for SkyShop (circuitous but buy time)

I can draft the provider ticket and the reroute steps. Recommend action B now + A in parallel.

Monica
Customer Solutions Manager // Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Li <anna@skyshop.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Nov 2028 09:48:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Sharp latency + 5xx on /checkout — urgent

Anna — quick update and request:

What we found so far (summary):
- Evidence points to a networking path issue (asymmetric hops + intermittent DNS timeouts) between SkyShop and our us-west edge POP.
- Proxy/NAT cluster at the peering handoff is returning connection resets that correlate with the 502s.

Ask: please confirm we have permission to share packet captures, traceroutes, and your request ids with the cloud provider and peering operator. Monica will open a provider ticket and request a temporary BGP reroute to an alternate POP.

Temporary mitigation: we can shift your traffic to a known-good POP (eu-1) for checkout traffic; there will be slightly increased RTT for EU users but it should restore throughput quickly. We will not make DNS changes on your behalf without explicit sign-off.

If you approve, we'll: 1) open provider ticket and share traces, 2) apply routing change for checkout traffic only, 3) monitor for restoration and roll back when stable.

Attachment: proposed_reroute_plan-1115.md (text/markdown)

Thanks — we'll standby for permission.

Rishi
Senior Account Lead // Redwood Inference

To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@skyshop.com, SkyShop CTO <cto@skyshop.com>

Current impact: checkout throughput down ~40% over the last 90m. Request id SKY-REQ-1123 attached to the logs. We'll accept temporary reroute to eu-1 ASAP.

PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/SKY-9876

Anna
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Nov 2028 17:30:00 -0800
Subject: Exec note: SkyShop checkout outage & next steps

Folks — final note after incident handoff:

Impact summary:
- Customer: SkyShop (payments)
- Impact window: 2028-11-15 09:00 PST -> mitigated by routing change at 09:58 PST; intermittent recurrences until 13:20 PST when provider implemented permanent route update.
- Business impact: estimated 40% checkout throughput drop during peak window (customer reports revenue impact).

What we did:
- Collected traces/pcap, identified asymmetric path + DNS timeouts at peering handoff.
- Requested provider reroute and applied temporary POP shift for checkout traffic.
- Restored baseline by 13:20 PST per provider ticket.

Actions for follow-up:
1) Commercial: review credit/compensation request and draft customer-facing exec summary (Marissa lead).
2) Technical: add automated path-health detection for high-volume accounts + an emergency BGP reroute runbook (Monica/Networking).
3) Post-incident: update SLO impact, ticketable lessons for product and SRE.

Marissa — pls prepare an executive note to SkyShop and a credit proposal. Monica — work with networking to formalize the runbook and add a playbook for provider engagement.

Vivek Kulkarni
